descriptionAdvanced.de: Shiney Row ist ein historisches Dorf im Metropolitan Borough der City of Sunderland, gelegen im Nordosten Englands. Der Name des Ortes ist Gegenstand vieler lokaler Legenden; einige behaupten, er beziehe sich auf das glänzende Erscheinungsbild der ersten Steinhäuser in einer Reihe. Die Entwicklung des Ortes im 19. Jahrhundert war fast ausschließlich auf den Kohlebergbau zurückzuführen, wobei die umliegenden Gruben wie Herrington und Philadelphia Tausenden von Menschen Arbeit gaben. Shiney Row war auch ein Zentrum der britischen Genossenschaftsbewegung, deren Einfluss noch heute im Ortsbild sichtbar ist. Nach der Schließung der Minen in den 1980er Jahren wandelte sich der Ort zu einem ruhigen Wohngebiet. Ein markantes Merkmal der Umgebung ist das nahegelegene Penshaw Monument, eine Nachbildung eines griechischen Tempels auf dem Penshaw Hill, das weithin sichtbar ist und einen spektakulären Blick über Tyne and Wear bietet.
descriptionAdvanced.hu: Shiney Row egy jellegzetes bányásztelepülés Sunderland közvetlen szomszédságában, Tyne and Wear megyében. A település nevét illetően több teória is létezik; a legnépszerűbb szerint a 'Shiney' (ragyogó) elnevezést az újonnan épült, tiszta kőházak sora után kapta, amely éles ellentétben állt a környező bányák porával. A falu gazdasági motorját évtizedekig a szénbányászat jelentette, a Philadelphia és Herrington bányák pedig meghatározták a helyi közösség identitását. Shiney Row jelentős szerepet játszott a helyi munkásmozgalomban és a szövetkezeti kereskedelemben is. A bányák bezárását követően a település zöldövezeti lakóhellyé alakult át. A látképet uralja a közeli Penshaw-dombon álló Penshaw-emlékmű, amely egy görög dór templom másolata, és Északkelet-Anglia egyik legismertebb jelképe.
descriptionAdvanced.ro: Shiney Row este o localitate pitorească aflată sub jurisdicția administrativă a orașului Sunderland, în regiunea Tyne and Wear. Istoria sa este strâns legată de epoca de aur a extracției cărbunelui din bazinul Durham, perioadă în care mica așezare s-a dezvoltat pentru a găzdui muncitorii de la minele din apropiere. Denumirea inedită de 'Shiney Row' (Șirul Strălucitor) se crede că provine de la aspectul ordonat și curat al primelor case din piatră construite pentru mineri. Pe lângă profilul industrial, localitatea a fost un punct focal pentru societățile cooperatiste, oferind un model de susținere comunitară. Astăzi, Shiney Row este o zonă rezidențială căutată, oferind echilibrul perfect între proximitatea urbană și accesul la peisaje naturale. Cel mai celebru vecin al său este monumentul Penshaw, o structură neoclasică impresionantă ridicată pe un deal adiacent în memoria lui Lord Durham.
descriptionAdvanced.en: Shiney Row is a prominent village in the City of Sunderland, located in the historic county of Durham. Its unique name is believed to originate from a row of newly built houses that appeared 'shiny' against the soot and grime of the surrounding industrial landscape. Throughout the 19th and early 20th centuries, the village thrived as a coal mining hub, with deep connections to the Herrington and Philadelphia collieries. The community was also a stronghold for the co-operative movement, and the Shiney Row Co-operative Society building remains an architectural highlight of the high street. Since the decline of the coal industry, Shiney Row has transitioned into a peaceful residential suburb. It is geographically defined by its proximity to the Penshaw Monument, a massive 19th-century Greek-style Doric temple that overlooks the village from its hilltop perch, serving as a landmark for the entire region.

en: The nearby Philadelphia pit was a major employer for over a century.
The Penshaw Monument was built in 1844 in memory of the 1st Earl of Durham.
Shiney Row sits just south of the River Wear valley.
St Oswald's Church is a significant Edwardian building completed in 1904.
The village was once served by the Lambton Colliery railway system.
It has one of the highest concentrations of historic co-operative buildings in the area.
